keyVerseText: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.
rootMeaning: The word εὐσεβῶς (eusebōs) is an adverb derived from the adjective εὐσεβής (eusebḗs), which means devout or godly, conveying a sense of well-reverence and piety. This root indicates not merely an outward appearance of religiosity but a deep, dutiful respect and reverence toward God, especially in fulfilling sacred duties. The literal sense enriches the common English gloss 'godly' by emphasizing active, reverent conduct grounded in sincere devotion.
usageInScripture: The term εὐσεβῶς appears only twice in the New Testament, consistently translated as 'godly,' which underscores a uniform understanding of the word as describing a lifestyle characterized by devoutness and reverence toward God. Its limited but focused usage highlights a consistent theme of piety expressed through righteous actions and attitudes. This consistency reveals that the biblical authors used the term to emphasize a godly way of living rather than a mere internal disposition or ritual formality.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding εὐσεβῶς in its original sense is vital for grasping the biblical call to a life marked by reverence and dutiful faithfulness to God. It points to a faith that is not passive but actively discharges sacred responsibilities in alignment with God's law and will. From an evangelical perspective, this word reminds believers that true godliness involves both inward devotion and outward obedience, reflecting Christ's own life and teachings. It challenges Christians to live out their faith in tangible, holy actions that honor God, reinforcing the transformative power of the gospel in daily conduct.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Timothy 3:12, the phrase 'all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution' uses εὐσεβῶς to describe a lifestyle marked by reverent and devout living. This word highlights that such a godly life is not easy or exempt from trials but is defined by faithful endurance in Christ. The term enriches the verse by emphasizing that godliness involves active, pious living that inevitably attracts opposition, yet remains steadfast in faith.
